text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.

- The Brussels conference on investment and trade in Croatia could contribute to resumption of the suspended talks on the country's cooperation with the EU, says head of the Belgian-Croatian Chamber of Commerce Willy de Clerq.
- Croatian electricity board (HEP) and the German RWE will set up a joint company to finance construction of the second thermal electric plant in Plomin, says HEP's director Damir Begovic.
- September industrial output up 4.8 percent from the same month last year. January-September output also up 2.5 percent from the previous year.
- Five new mass graves found near Sanski Most in northwest Bosnia, containing more than 100 bodies, including those of babies in diapers.
- Stock exchange commentary: Are bears lurking? The end of last week slowed down the price stampede.
- State statistics bureau suffers from a shortage of skilled staff needed to improve research, says its head Ivan Rusan.
- International auditors Coopers&Lybrand found a joint firm in Croatia with Zagreb's Revicon.

- State post and telecomms company HPT tops the list of 1995 profit-makers with 331.8 million kuna after-tax. Followed by Pliva with 229.1 million. Brewery Daruvarska Pivovara the best with a 27.2 percent ratio of profit to total revenues.
- Stjepan Brolich replaces Kresimir Beno at the head of the national reserves. A commission to be appointed by parliament to investigate the so-called 'wheat' affair.
- Zagreb crisis: following the resignation of some opposition members, the ruling HDZ says it will soon have a majority in the city assembly to appoint a mayor from its ranks.
- Catholic Church will get little or nothing under the new law on denationalisation of property, says the legal representative of the Zagreb Archbishopric Zvjezdna Znidarcic-Begovic.
- Private food concern Agrokor d.d. says it has lost 1.2 million German marks for exporting 150,000 tonnes of wheat from state reserves.
- Insurer Zagreb increased its market share to 5.44 percent in 1996, climbing to the second place just behind the biggest, Croatia Osiguranje.
- Only privatisation can prevent a collapse of Croatia's pension system, says Peter Young, director of the London's Adam Smith Institute.
- September total jobless up 2.4 percent from August and up 9.2 percent from the same month last year. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
